claims.claim: The European Union banned the use of antibiotics as growth promoters in animal feed effective 2006.
claims.episode_span: The European Union banned antibiotic growth promoters in animal feed in 2006
claims.supporting_quote: The European Union banned the use of antibiotics as growth agents starting on 1 January 2006 with Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003.

claims.claim: Antimicrobial resistance is estimated to be directly responsible for about 1.27 million deaths worldwide per year (2019 estimate).
claims.episode_span: contributing to an estimated 1.27 million deaths worldwide each year
claims.supporting_quote: estimating that bacterial AMR was directly responsible for 1.27 million global deaths in 2019 and contributed to over 4 million deaths in 2021.

claims.claim: Alexander Fleming first observed penicillin's antibacterial effect in 1928 while working at St Mary's Hospital in London.
claims.episode_span: Alexander Fleming had noticed the effect in 1928 while working at St. Mary’s Hospital in London
claims.supporting_quote: While working at St Mary's Hospital in London in 1928, Scottish physician Alexander Fleming was the first to show experimentally that a Penicillium mould secretes an antibacterial substance, which he named "penicillin".

claims.claim: The first therapeutic administration of purified penicillin was to Oxford policeman Albert Alexander, beginning on 12 February 1941, for a severe facial infection.
claims.episode_span: The first human trial occurred on 12 February 1941 when Florey’s team administered penicillin to Albert Alexander
claims.supporting_quote: Fletcher next identified an Oxford policeman, Albert Alexander , who had a severe facial infection involving streptococci and staphylococci which had developed from a small sore at the corner of his mouth. His whole face, eyes and scalp were swollen to the extent that he had an eye removed to relieve the pain. [ 88 ] [ 89 ] On 12 February, Fletcher administered 200 mg of penicillin, following by 100 mg doses every three hours.

claims.claim: In his Nobel lecture Fleming warned that underdosing penicillin could make microbes resistant, in the words quoted by the episode.
claims.episode_span: “there is the danger that the ignorant man may easily underdose himself and by exposing his microbes to non-lethal quantities of the drug make them resistant,”
claims.supporting_quote: In his Nobel lecture, Fleming warned of the possibility of penicillin resistance in clinical conditions: The time may come when penicillin can be bought by anyone in the shops. Then there is the danger that the ignorant man may easily underdose himself and by exposing his microbes to non-lethal quantities of the drug make them resistant.

claims.claim: The first methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) isolates were reported in Britain in 1961, shortly after methicillin's introduction.
claims.episode_span: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus emerged in a British hospital in 1961, only two years after methicillin’s introduction
claims.supporting_quote: In 1961, the first known MRSA isolates were reported in a British study, and from 1961 to 1967, infrequent hospital outbreaks occurred in Western Europe and Australia,

claims.claim: The New Delhi metallo-beta-lactamase (NDM-1) carbapenem-resistance gene was first detected in 2008, in Klebsiella pneumoniae.
claims.episode_span: carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae carrying New Delhi metallo-beta-lactamase genes first identified in 2008
claims.supporting_quote: NDM-1 was first detected in 2008 in a culture plate of Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from a Swedish patient of Indian origin.
